I was once awake and active for a 4 day weekend.

It was the first paintball scenario I was involved in creating.

Got up Thursday morning went to the field. Started coordinating things and setting up. Spent the afternoon making props. The night was all laminating pre-registration ID cards and stuffing envelopes with the game info.

Friday morning, most of the regular staff (judges) showed up to work on the field. I spent the day coordinating where everything needed to go and briefing the Staff on how things would run, and making sure they all knew the special rules.

Friday night. I finished up the last registration packs, and relaxed at a dinner with with friends and "senior staff".

Saturday morning was registration. Game began at Noon and ran all night. 28 Hours straight. The senior staff and I rotated jobs. There was the Mission Mister, handing out missions and keeping score. Supreme Justice, to organise the judges, answer questions and resolve major player disputes. The Black Market, to buy and sell props, and help keep the game balanced. Finally the Master of Stories ran the role playing scenario aspects.

The game ended around 4pm on Sunday. Closing ceremonies, announcing scores and giving special awards and acknowledgements. Clean up, followed by judges party for dinner.

That night, I slept for nearly 13 hours straight. I usually have trouble sleeping for more than 4-5 hours at a time, so that was kind of miraculous for me.

Back when in basic training in the army we had a week long sleep deprivation exercise. Basically a normal exercise but at all the points where you would normally get your sleep in, we would be either moved out on a patrol or be forced to move out of location. It wasn't as if we were just sitting there 'trying' to stay awake or so engrossed in something we didn't even notice the time fly. It was constant movement and a buffet of bullshit. Every time you would think you could sneak in a quick 5 min power nap (ie your shell scrape is dug, admin is squared away, not much to do now) you would again be attacked, sent on patrol, put on guard or moved to a new location.
After around the 4th day (that is a vague measurement as to be honest the days just blended into each other after a while) we were allowed to sneak in the occasional 30 min or so sleep, and that was it. It is still amazing to me that back then a 5 min nap in a muddy wet ditch felt like a full nights sleep in a bed made of angel hair and puppies. I remember a lot of it was just zombie like. You did stuff because you were told to or you were trained to. A lot of auto-pilot stuff. You were constantly angry at everyone. Hours blended. To be honest a lot of it i just don't remember due to it being just a blur. I remember key things or events. I also remember getting back to base and falling asleep in the bathtub and nearly drowning and then driving back home for the weekend post-exercise leave and falling asleep at the wheel. I remember the hallucinations and vaguely remember some of the points that my brain just shut down and i would fall asleep standing up.

Not something i would like to do again. But definitely something i chuckle about when i remember it.
